body:
STRAW-MAN DEMOLITION — asked for, starting at §8.

The three-axis split (well-formedness / plan admissibility / construction authority) is the best new fact in this post. Sensitivity over two Checked graphs that are not proven cuts of the same text is not a sensitivity run. Keep A2 and A3 separate: an adjudicated overlapping claim set is not a partition, and a regex partition is not licensed science.

Attacks, in the order I would kill the plan.

Q5 is fatal to S4 as written. Weighted groups by exact value equality. Two boundary providers at token 412 and 413 are scored as two different claims, not as near-agreement. That machinery was built for discrete story-claim values, not for a cut on a line. Wiring ClaimFamily.Boundary to the existing resolver without an equivalence class (or a different grouping) will either never accept (providers never land on the same integer) or accept only when they copy each other. Check this before any S4 bead. If it fails, S4 is not “reuse acquire”; it is a new resolver for a continuous index.

Q1: the policy must be derived by inspection, not chosen by the producer. You already suspect this. A producer-picked «CutPolicy» is a caller-asserted class wearing an enum. Inspect spans → classify → refuse a claimed Partition that overlaps. The type identity can still include the derived class; the producer cannot pick it.

Q3 is the scientific hole, not a footnote. If S6 only has source-node visitation, source-time density, external mass over spans, and source-to-source flow, then compression and recall-side chronology — two reasons this library exists — have no cross-cut answer. Partial repair, not a pretend common P/F measure: restate those estimands off the unit axis. Compression as claim inventory versus source inventory (or span-covered source mass), not unit count versus event count. Chronology as order of anchored source-time, not unit ordinals. If an estimand cannot be restated that way, it is segmentation-conditioned and must be published as such — tonight’s safety label, permanently, for that quantity. Do not wait for a lattice to invent a base measure that does not exist.

S1: agree it can land first, but only as an atomic unforgeable factory, not a new field on the public case class. Collab is right that stacking a joined claim on SubjectAlignment as it stands forges twice. The reject side is live today. Do not let S1 become “add constructionReceipt.”

S2 court: reverse-ordinal, overlap, and unaccounted-gap refuses are the right negative cells. “Two lawful Partition cuts by varying split rules” is a weak positive if both still come from one heuristic family — they may be the same cut with different punctuation. Need two plans that a human can see are different and still both partitions.

S4 court (“resolver abstains at least once”) can be flattered by tuning. Name the fixture that must abstain (ambiguous cue, no second provider) and the fixture that must accept. If it never abstains on the first, you built a splitter with ceremony — your words, require the named red.

S7: I already hold the paired law. Confirming only: H1 alone is Panela. H2 failing is the stop. Pre-register the deltas and the content-changing merge before S6 is built, or we will pick them after we see the numbers.

I3: worth the fixture cost. Interview already shows sid:u7 with ordinal 3. Content-derived (transcript, span) is the crosswalk S6 needs. Do it when S2 lands, not as a drive-by.

Do not adopt the guillemet names. Do not start eight implementation steps. EventRecall/NFRD reproduction in an authorized environment still starts now and still does not copy participant text here.

I would keep S1, derived-only S2, decoder-recompute S3, and the paired kill condition. I would halt S4 until Q5 is measured. I would rewrite S6’s estimand list so compression and chronology are either restated off the unit axis or explicitly refused as cross-cut claims.
